title: dynamic-kv-partitioning-for-cross-split-gpu-topologies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal: introduce a runtime-driven dynamic KV partitioning layer that maps variable-sized KV micro-shards to GPU memory slices according to both tensor and pipeline parallel topology. Unlike static stripe/band strategies, this approach continuously adapts shard placement using a lightweight telemetry stream (access frequency, TTL, resident-set sizes) and a low-cost migration protocol that prefers intra-node peer-to-peer transfers and batched RDMA when available. Goals: reduce peak memory pressure on overloaded GPUs, bound cross-GPU bandwidth used for KV operations, and limit tail latency regressions under bursty prompt patterns. Key features: (1) Micro-shard metadata catalogue (fixed 2–16 KB shard units) to make movement cheap; (2) Hotspot steering where frequently accessed micro-shards are replicated to neighboring devices with ephemeral leases; (3) Lazy migration + shadow-copy consistency to avoid blocking generation; (4) Topology-aware placement that prefers colocating shards with the pipeline stage that emits/consumes them most; (5) Eviction policy augmented with per-request density heuristics to avoid oscillation under flash crowds. Trade-offs: added cross-GPU traffic and metadata overhead vs. reduced OOMs and lower 99.9th latency. This ticket covers design, a prototype runtime hook, and evaluation on heterogeneous 8xA100 and 4xH100 clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype integrates with runtime plugin points and can migrate micro-shards between GPUs without blocking generation
Observed reduction in OOM events by >= 60% on synthetic hotspot workload compared to static tiling baseline
99th and 99.9th token latency regression <= 10% for standard chat workload at production QPS
Network egress for KV migration under steady-state < 12% of baseline inter-GPU bandwidth
Comprehensive doc and an RFC merged, plus at least one end-to-end benchmark in CI (perf/regression)
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Initial spike: defined micro-shard size candidates (2KB, 8KB, 16KB) and prototype migration handshake. WIP design doc uploaded.

2026-02-23 - Liam OConnor: Ran first synthetic hotspot test on 8xA100. Static partitioning OOM at high concurrency; prototype with replication avoids OOM but doubles bandwidth. Need smarter lease expiration.
2026-02-28 - Marco Reyes (review): Suggested topology hints from pipeline scheduler to reduce cross-stage fetches. Also recommended batched async memcpy using CUDA IPC where possible.

2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Implemented lazy shadow-copy: new owner installs shadow pointer while source continues serving for one epoch. Observed <2% error rate in synchronization tests; fixed race by adding epoch barriers to publish metadata.

2026-03-07 - QA (Denise Chang): Stability run: 24-hour mixed workload. OOMs dropped 72% vs baseline, but tail latency increased 14% on the busiest tenant. Next step: throttle migrations during tail-surge windows and add tenant-aware priority.
2026-03-09 - Liam OConnor: Opened PR #2567 with core migration loop and telemetry buffer. Needs performance optimization of metadata catalog lookups (hot-path).

2026-03-10 - Product (Ravi Kumar): Confirmed customer beta for an enterprise tenant with heavy conversational deduping. Requested observability metrics: per-shard residency timeline and migration counters exposed in Console.
